title: budgeter: org spend lockdown — alerts + scp circuit breaker via declastruct
description:
## .what

give the budgeter role (a stub today) a paved org spend lockdown: alerts plus a hard circuit
breaker, declared via declastruct, applied as the org manager.

## .why

an org needs a ceiling it cannot cross by accident. ahbode has alerts only; nheuron now has both,
and the pattern is generic. reference: rhachet-roles-nheuron
`provision/aws.budget/account=.root/resources.ts` + `getAllAdminEmails.ts`.

## .the shape

- one org-wide monthly COST budget in the management account, `costFilters: null` (consolidated
  billing covers every member)
- alerts: ACTUAL > warn mark, FORECASTED > ceiling, ACTUAL > ceiling
- breaker: `DeclaredAwsBudgetAction` kind `APPLY_SCP_POLICY`, AUTOMATIC, at the ceiling, attaches
  a deny-all SCP (NotAction allowlist: billing, budgets, ce, sts, sso, iam/org reads, support)
- **one breaker budget per member account.** aws binds an SCP action to ONE target, and
  declastruct allows one action of each kind per budget — so each member gets a twin budget at
  the same org-wide ceiling to carry its breaker
- an execution role trusted by `budgets.amazonaws.com`, plus an inline grant for
  `organizations:AttachPolicy` / `DetachPolicy` (the declastruct-aws demo role has the trust
  policy only)
- alert recipients read live from identity center: every user who holds the admin permission
  set on the management account. no address in git or keyrack; the list follows the roster

## .limits to state in the brief

- aws evaluates budgets a few times a day and bill data lags hours: spend can pass the ceiling
  before the freeze lands
- an SCP never binds the management account — keep it free of workloads
- the freeze blocks new calls, not resources that already accrue; aws lifts it next period
